newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-KLINSMANN GOAL HELPS BAYERN STRETCH LEAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KLINSMANN GOAL HELPS BAYERN STRETCH LEAD.

text.p: Bayern Munich extended their Bundesliga lead to three points on Saturday, a Juergen Klinsmann goal earning them a 1-1 draw at Bochum.
Defender Torsten Kracht put Bochum ahead in the 55th minute. Klinsmann struck his eighth goal of the season, from close range, 10 minutes later.

Bayern were left to rue a string of missed second half chances to clinch the game and establish a five-point cushion over second-placed Borussia Dortmund, who lost 2-0 at Fortuna Duessldorf on Friday.
Off-form midfielder Mehmet Scholl was the main culprit, scorning two great opportunities inside 15 minutes.
"If Scholl hadn't been so selfish, we could have won," Bayern coach Giovanni Trapattoni said. "But I don't blame him. He just wants to score a goal because he's being criticised at the moment."
Third-placed Bayer Leverkusen and fourth-placed VfB Stuttgart took the chance to close the gap on the top two with hard-fought home wins.

Christian Woerns capitalised on a goalmouth scramble in the 36th minute to score Leverkusen's goal in their 1-0 victory over Duisburg. The win brought Leverkusen level on points with Dortmund but the champions have a superior goal difference.
"Only the win counts for us, although it was a tough game," said Leverkusen coach Christoph Daum, who has turned his side from last season's relegation candidates to title challengers.
VfB Stuttgart, who began the season in outstanding form but have failed to manage a win in their last four games, bounced back with a 1-0 win over local rivals Karlsruhe.
Germany striker Fredi Bobic headed home a corner from Bulgarian playmaker Krassimir Balakov in the final minute to steal all three points for Stuttgart in a pulsating match.

"We're disappointed to have lost a goal in the last minute," said Karlsruhe trainer Winfried Schaefer, whose side dumped Bayern out of the German Cup in midweek. "The team deserved more from the game than they got."
Werder Bremen held on for a 1-0 win over relegation-threatened Hansa Rostock, despite having Dieter Eilts sent off for persistent fouling in the 27th minute.
"We came under enormous pressure after Eilts was sent off but we held firm in defence," said Bremen coach Hans-Juergen Doerner.
